Q: A python function that finds a number's largest divisor excluding itself A:

This problem arises when n is a prime number as you exclude n from it. (That is n is not divisible by anyother numbers except 1 and self(n).

The easiest way to find if a number is prime is: Get the square root of n. Ignore decimals(Take only int part). assume this number as m. If the number is not prime, then n will be divisible by at least one of the numbers in the range(2, m+1).

def is_prime(n):
    m = n**(0.5)
    m = int(m)
    if n < 2: return False
    for i in range(2, m + 1):
        if n%i == 0: return False
    return True

As you want the largest divisor, you can iterate backwards so unnecessary iterations can be avoided. Also the starting number can be from approximately half of n because when it is not a prime number, the minimum smallest divisor could be 2.

def largestDivisor(n):
    if is_prime(n): return f"{n} is a prime number"

    # if n is even starting num should be (n+1)/2 and if even st should be ((n+1)/2) + 1
    st = (n/2)+ 1 if n%2 == 0 else ((n+1)/2) + 1

    # iterate backwards with step -1
    for i in range(st, 1, -1):
        if n%i == 0: return n

Q: Gekko in a Docker Container A:

Here is a tutorial on how to Dockerize a Python program that is run from a Command Line Interface (CLI). Include gekko in the requirements.txt file. This uses a minimal version of Python that is designed for docker containers.

FROM python:3.9-slim
RUN useradd --create-home --shell /bin/bash app_user
WORKDIR /home/app_user
COPY requirements.txt ./
USER app_user
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
CMD ["bash"]

There is also a two part series on how to package applications in a Docker container with Part 1 - Using Docker Desktop and Docker Hub and How to Build and Test Your Docker Images in the Cloud with Docker Hub.

A few things to consider:

  • Include m.path (GEKKO run-time directory) in the Docker PATH: Compiling Gekko with Pyinstaller The m._path value can be changed from the tmp directory to something else.
  • More information about the Gekko run directory: Gekko Python: Any way to export the model for debugging purposes?
  • The Gekko GUI requires Flask webserver and other components to run: How do I display solution in GEKKO GUI? This will increase the size and complexity of the Docker container.
  • Include communication protocols such as Modbus or OPC UA to read and write values to and from a Programmable Logic Controller or Distributed Control System.

Every MPC application that I've created is so customized with a particular model for a particular application that it doesn't seem practical to create a general-purpose Docker container. If the application can be developed once and copied to many similar systems (e.g. MPC to replace PID control) then a Docker container may make sense to ease deployment.

Q: Could the L1 Cache Save Computation Time? A:

Awesome work, Interceptor TSK!

This post was a reference to a question that I asked that got deleted from StackOverflow. The question was about whether logical operators like NAND do the job more quickly than an adder circuit, since the adder has to use the carry bits to calculate the next bit in the sum. One of the answers that I got was that there are adders that can compute the sum in almost O(1) time, rendering this unnecessary.

Speedups would definitely be needed for multiplication (which is done by performing repeated additions). If one can find the most significant bit in each factor, then you can check to see how many bits the product contains. A product shorter than 16 bits (255^2 = (2^8)^2 = 2^16) can be computed using 16–bit registers, which are still used by Intel processors for backwards compatibility.

Once again, thank you for putting in the time to test this idea. I should have a solution written soon!

Q: Fortran subroutine not returning the expected value A:

After calling the subroutine the abbreviation is blank though there is no error.

Yes, because the function never modifies the value of month_abb. Possibly you meant to include something like this before the print statement:

    month_abb = months(month_num)

Side note: 99 is greater than 12, so when the user enters 99 to end the program, they will first get the "Invalid Entry for Month, Try again" message. You can avoid that by performing the test for 99 and conditional exit first.
